### 1. CalFresh (SNAP) – What It Is

column1: #### Basic Eligibility (keeps changing, so check your county)
- **Income:** Usually ≤ 200 % of the federal poverty level (about $2,900 /month for a single adult in 2025).

Q_002,Can I recieve multiple types of assistance at the same time?,## Yes – You can often get **more than one** public‑assistance program at the same time
Most California programs let you receive help from **different sources** together.
But each program has its own rules about who can get it, how much you can earn, and what you must tell them about other benefits.
## How the programs work together

column4: Yes – can be combined with Medi‑Cal, CalWORKs, SSI, GA, LIHEAP, etc.
column5: Report any income (including unemployment) so they can check the limits.

column3: Health care
column4: Yes – can be combined with CalFresh, SSI, GA, etc.
column5: No extra reporting needed unless your income changes.

column3: Cash help for families with children
column4: Yes – can be combined with CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, LIHEAP, etc.
column5: Must report any other cash benefits you receive.

column3: Cash help for adults without children
column4: Yes – can be combined with CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, SSI, LIHEAP, etc.
column5: Must report all other income and benefits.

column3: Money for seniors, blind or disabled
column4: Yes – can be combined with Medi‑Cal, CalFresh, GA, etc.
column5: SSI is a separate federal program; you still must tell other agencies about the money you get.

column3: Help paying heating/electric bills
column4: Yes – can be combined with any cash‑or‑food program.

column3: Housing, nutrition, or veteran aid

column1: **Bottom line:**
- You can “stack” benefits, but **always tell every program about the others**.
- Some programs have **income limits**; if one benefit pushes your income above a limit, the other program might reduce its payment.
## Steps to Apply for Multiple Programs
1. **Gather needed papers** (see the checklist below).
2. **Contact your county Human Services Agency (HSA)** – they can help you apply for several programs at once.
3. **Fill out the application** for each program (many can be done online, by phone, or in person).
4. **Submit the paperwork** and wait for the agency to review it.
5. **Tell each program** once you are approved for a new benefit.

### Typical timelines

**10‑30 days** (most counties aim for 30 days).

## County‑Specific Note
California counties run the day‑to‑day administration of these programs.
- **Application forms, office hours, and processing speed can differ** from one county to another.
- Some counties have **online portals** (e.g., “BenefitsCal”) while others require an in‑person visit.
**What to do:**
Call or visit your **county Human Services Agency** website. Look for “Apply for CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, CalWORKs, GA, SSI assistance” on the site.
## Other Programs You Might Want to Explore
Even if you didn’t ask about them, they often go hand‑in‑hand with the main benefits:

## Quick Checklist for You
- [ ] Call **your county Human Services Agency** or visit their website.
- [ ] Collect the documents listed above.
- [ ] Ask the clerk if you can **apply for several programs at once** (they often have a “combined application” packet).
- [ ] Fill out each application truthfully and **report all other benefits you receive**.
- [ ] Keep copies of everything you submit.
- [ ] Follow up if you haven’t heard back after **30 days**.

Losing a job is stressful, but many Californians are able to get food, health care, and cash help while they look for new work. Keep asking questions, stay organized, and let the county staff know about any changes in your income or household. They’re there to help you get the support you need.

You can definitely apply for CalFresh if you just lost your job. If your income recently stopped, your county will only count any final payments you got in the last 30 days to calculate how much CalFresh you will receive in the first month. If you still have any income, your ongoing benefits will be based only on that income, not income that has stopped. You should provide proof of any money you got in the last 30 days if you can.

It isn't required, but it can be helpful to provide any proof you have that your income has stopped. This could be a letter, or a screenshot of an email or text from your employer that explains that you are no longer working. ### Basic Eligibility Checklist
You will need to meet **all** of the following to receive UI benefits:
- **Totally or partially unemployed** through **no fault of your own** (e.g., layoff, reduced hours).
- **Physically able** to work.
- **Available for work** and **actively looking** each week.
- **Ready and willing** to accept suitable work right away.
- **Social Security Number** and legal authorization to work in the U.S.
- **Enough wages** in the base period (the EDD will calculate this for you).
### Steps to Find Out If You Qualify
1. **Gather your wage records** (pay stubs, W‑2s, 1099s) from the last 18 months.
2. **Create an UI Online account** at the [Employment Development Department (EDD) website](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/).
3. **Start a new claim** – the system will automatically pull your earnings from state wage records and tell you if you meet the base‑period requirement.
4. **Complete the weekly certification** once you’re approved, confirming you’re still looking for work.

## 3. How to Apply for Medi‑Cal
1. **Gather Your Documents** (you’ll need them for any program)
- Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
- Social Security number (or proof you don’t have one)
- Recent pay stubs, unemployment benefits statement, or a letter showing loss of income
- Proof of household size (lease, utility bill, or school enrollment for kids)
- Immigration documents (green card, work permit, or other status proof)
2. **Apply Online** – Go to the **[CA Benefits portal](https://www.mybenefits.calhub.org)** and create an account. The online form walks you through each question.
3. **Apply In‑Person or By Phone**
- Call **County Human Services Agency** (your county’s name + “Human Services” – e.g., “Los Angeles County Human Services”).
- Visit a **County Social Services Office**. Staff can help you fill out the application and verify documents.
4. **Submit Your Application** – After you send it, a caseworker will review it (usually **within 30 days**).
5. **Get a Decision** – If approved, you’ll receive a **Medi‑Cal ID card** (often within 2‑3 weeks).
### Quick Tips
- **Apply right away** – Even if you’re not sure you meet the income limit, you can still apply; the agency will tell you.
- **Don’t wait for your unemployment benefits** – You can apply while you’re waiting for the check.
- **Keep copies** of everything you submit; it helps if there are any follow‑up questions.

Q_011,Laid off this month. I need help paying for food. Can I get help quickly? What can I qualify for and how do I apply in my county?,## You Can Get Food Help Quickly

You’ve just been laid off, and that can be scary. The good news is that **CalFresh** (California’s food stamp program) can start helping you right away, and there are other safety‑net services you may qualify for.
## What Is CalFresh?

column3: Who can get it

column2: Gives a monthly cash card to buy groceries
column3: Individuals or families with low or no income. You must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or have an eligible immigration status.
column4: The county has **up to 30 days** to decide. If you have very low income and few resources, they may **expedite** the case (often within 1–2 weeks).

column1: ### Why you still qualify after a layoff
- Your county will only count any *final pay* you received in the **last 30 days**.
- Ongoing benefits are based on the income you have **now** (which may be zero).
- You don’t need a fancy proof that you’re out of work, but a short note from your former employer or a personal letter helps the county see your situation.
## How to Apply in Your County
1. **Start the online application** – go to **[BenefitsCal.com](https://benefitscal.com)** and click **“Apply for CalFresh.”**
2. **Create a login** (you’ll need an email address).
3. **Fill out the form** – answer questions about who lives with you, your income, assets, and any benefits you already receive.
4. **Submit supporting documents** (see table below).
5. **Eligibility interview** – your county will call you within **1‑2 weeks** to set up a phone or in‑person interview.
6. **Wait for a decision** – most counties give a decision within **30 days**; ask for “expedited” if you have a very low income.

## What Happens After You’re Approved?
- You’ll receive an **EBT card** in the mail (usually within a few days of approval).
- The first month’s benefit amount is based on the pay you earned in the last 30 days.
- Each month the county will recalculate based on any new income you report.
## Other Help You May Need Right Now

column1: ## Quick Checklist Before You Call
- Write down **your full name, address, phone, and Social Security number**.
- Have a **list of who lives with you** (adults, children, seniors).
- Gather any **pay stubs, termination notice, or a short letter** explaining you were laid off.
- Keep a **photo ID** and a **utility bill or lease** handy.
When you call your county Social Services office, you can say:
> “I was laid off this month and need help with food. I’d like to apply for CalFresh and would like an expedited interview if possible.”
The person on the line will guide you through the next steps and give you the phone number for your local office.
## Remember
- **You are not alone.** Many Californians apply for CalFresh after a job loss, and the system is set up to start helping quickly.
- **Eligibility rules can vary a little by county**, so the exact documents or interview timing may differ. The county staff will tell you exactly what they need.

Q_015,Can you explain how unemployment insurance works and how to maximize what I can receive?,## How Unemployment Insurance (UI) Works
Unemployment Insurance is a **temporary cash benefit** for workers in California who lost their job (or had hours cut) **through no fault of their own**.

column2: Gives you a weekly payment while you look for work or go to training

• You are **physically able, available, and looking for work** each week
column4: The weekly amount is a percentage of your past earnings.  California’s calculator (on the EDD website) shows an estimate, but the exact number is decided when your claim is processed.  Payments can range from about **$40 – $450 per week**.

column1: > **Note:** The exact benefit amount, any additional training supplements, and the length of time you can receive benefits may **vary by county** and by your work history.
## Basic Eligibility Checklist

column3: What it means for you
You need a valid SSN.
If you’re not a U.S. citizen, you must have work authorization.
Your wages during the “base period” must meet the state’s minimum.

column2: **Unemployed through no fault of your own**

## Step‑by‑Step to Apply
1. **Gather Your Information**
- Social Security number
- Driver’s license or ID number
- Complete work history for the last 18 months (employer names, dates, wages)
- Recent pay stubs or W‑2 forms (helpful but not required)
2. **Apply Online** – Go to the EDD’s UI portal at **[edd.ca.gov/unemployment](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/)** and start a new claim.
3. **Register on CalJOBS** – Within 7 days of filing, create a CalJOBS account and upload a resume.
4. **Complete the Initial Interview**
- A staff member may call you for a brief interview to confirm details.
- Be ready to answer questions about your last job, reason for separation, and availability.
5. **Review Benefit Documents**
- You’ll receive a **Notice of Determination** (DE 1080CZ) telling you if you’re approved and the weekly amount.
6. **Start Certifying Weekly**
- Log in to **UI Online** (via myEDD) each week and answer the simple “yes/no” questions about work search and earnings.
7. **Receive Payments**
- First payment usually arrives **about 3 weeks** after your claim is approved.
- Payments are deposited onto a debit card or into your bank account.
8. **Keep Certifying Until Benefits End**
- Continue weekly certifications. If you find a job, you must tell the EDD right away.

Q_018,Where can I get help finding a job in California after a layoff, and do they connect to benefits?","## 🌟 You’re Not Alone – Help Is Here!

Losing a job can feel scary, but California has a lot of free services that help you **find new work** and **connect you to cash, food, or training benefits**. Below is a simple guide written at a 5‑th‑grade reading level.
## 1. Main Places to Get Job‑Finding Help

column3: What It Does
column4: How to Start
column5: Who Can Use It

column3: Free one‑stop centers that help you write a resume, practice interviews, search job listings, and sign up for training. Many centers also have staff who can answer questions about unemployment insurance (UI) and other benefits.
column4: Find your nearest center on the **[EDD Job Center map](https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs_and_training/)** or call 1‑800‑388‑9373. Walk in; no appointment is needed.
column5: Anyone who lives in California and is looking for work, including those who were laid off.

column3: Online portal where you can create a resume, search thousands of jobs, and apply for training programs. Registration is required to keep UI benefits.
column4: Go to **[CalJOBS.org](https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs_and_training/Caljobs/)**, click **“Create Account,”** and follow the prompts.
column5: All job seekers, especially those receiving UI benefits.

column3: County‑specific groups that run job‑training programs, apprenticeship opportunities, and “Rapid Response” services for layoffs.
column4: Search **“Workforce Development Board + [your county]”** or ask at an AJCC.
column5: Residents of the county; many programs target workers who lost a job in the last 12 months.

column3: Special help for veterans, including resume workshops and connections to employer partners.
column4: Visit the **[EDD Veterans page](https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs_and_training/Veterans/)** or your local VA office.
column5: Veterans and eligible family members.

column3: Job‑placement counselors, assistive technology, and employer outreach focused on disability inclusion.
column4: Call the **EDD Disability Services line 1‑800‑480‑3287** or ask at an AJCC.
column5: Californians with a disability that makes finding work harder.

column1: ### Do These Services Connect to Benefits?

* When you register on **CalJOBS**, the system automatically notifies the Employment Development Department (EDD) that you are looking for work. That keeps your **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** payments flowing.
* Many AJCCs have a **Benefits Navigator** who can help you complete applications for **UI, CalWORKs, CalFresh (food stamps), and California Training Benefits** on the spot.
* Your County **Social Services Agency** (the office that runs CalWORKs & CalFresh) works closely with AJCCs, so you can often do both job‑search and benefits paperwork in the same place.
## 2. Quick Steps After a Layoff

column3: What to Do
column4: Why It Matters

column3:
• Recent pay stubs (last 4 weeks)
• Your last employer’s name, address, and phone
• Reason you’re not working (layoff)
• Your Social Security #
• Driver’s license or ID
column4: Needed for UI and other benefit applications.

column3: Go to **[EDD UI Online (myEDD)](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/)** and create an account. The application takes ~15 min.

column3: After you apply for UI, the EDD will send a “Notice to Register” (usually within 7‑10 days). Log in to **CalJOBS.org** and post a resume within 21 days.
column4: Keeps UI benefits active; you’ll see job matches right away.

column3: Bring your UI claim number and ID. Ask for a **Benefits Navigator** and a **Job Counselor**.
column4: Gets you help with resume, interview prep, and any other benefits you may qualify for.

column3: Ask about **California Training Benefits** (you can take classes while still getting UI). Look for free community‑college courses, apprenticeships, or industry‑specific certifications.
column4: Improves your chances of getting a better job faster.

column3: Every two weeks, log in to myEDD and answer the UI certification questions (“Did you look for work?”).
column4: Guarantees you keep receiving UI payments.

column3: Check emails or mail from the EDD and your county Social Services office. If you get a notice to give more info, respond quickly (usually within 10 days).
column4: Avoids delays or pauses in benefits.

## 4. How Long Does It Take?

column3: Typical Time Frame
About **3‑4 weeks** after you finish the first certification.
**Same day** if you have internet; remember the 21‑day deadline.
Walk‑in help is immediate; workshops run weekly or monthly.

## 5. County‑Specific Note

- **Every California county has its own Social Services Agency** that runs CalWORKs and CalFresh. Application forms are the same, but **appointment wait times, document requirements, and processing speeds can differ**.

- If you live in a **rural county**, you might need to travel a short distance to the nearest AJCC or county office. Some counties offer **online video appointments**—ask the Benefits Navigator about that option.
## 6. Other Programs You Might Find Helpful

## 7. Quick Checklist (Print or Write It Down)
- [ ] **Apply for UI** on myEDD (online ASAP)
- [ ] **Register on CalJOBS** within 21 days of the notice
- [ ] **Visit the nearest AJCC** – bring ID, UI claim #, and any pay stubs
- [ ] **Ask for a Benefits Navigator** (UI, CalWORKs, CalFresh, CTB)
- [ ] **Gather documents** (ID, pay stubs, termination notice, residence proof)
- [ ] **Set a weekly reminder** to certify UI every two weeks
- [ ] **Write down** each job search activity (applications, contacts, workshops)
### You’ve Got This!

California’s workforce system is built to help people like you get back to work **and** keep money coming in while you do it. Take one step at a time, use the free resources at your local AJCC, and don’t hesitate to ask for help—you deserve support. 🌈

Q_027,I was laid off, have kdis, and savings are low. For food stamps, can I get faster help and how does UI or severance affect eligibility? I might move countise soon to live with my mom to save money—what changes?","## Quick Help — Getting Food Stamps (CalFresh) Right Away
**You can apply for CalFresh now and still receive your unemployment benefits (UI).**
If the money you get from UI is **not higher than CalFresh’s income limits**, you can get both programs at the same time.

column3: Why it matters

column2: **Fastest way:** Apply online through your county’s CalFresh portal or call the county office.
column3: Online apps are processed as quickly as possible – many people get a decision in **7‑10 days**.

column2: **Proof of income:** Show any UI payments you already receive (or a notice that you’ve applied). If you haven’t gotten UI money yet, you **don’t have to report it** on the CalFresh form right now.
column3: The county will only count income you actually receive.

column2: **Severance pay:** If you got a one‑time severance check, you must tell the county. It will be counted as **income for the month you receive it** and may lower your CalFresh amount for that month only.
column3: One‑time money is treated like regular earnings, but it won’t affect future months once it’s used up.

column2: **Moving to a new county:** When you move, you’ll need to **re‑apply or transfer** your CalFresh case to the new county. The new county may have slightly different paperwork or wait times.
column3: Each county runs its own CalFresh program, so you’ll have to let the new county know you’re moving.

column1: ### How to Apply (step‑by‑step)
1. **Gather needed documents**
- Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
- Proof of residence (lease, utility bill, or a letter from your mom if you’ll stay with her)
- Social Security numbers for you and each child
- Recent UI award notice or a copy of the UI claim you filed
- Any severance check or pay stub (if you have one)
2. **Start the application**
- Go to your **county’s CalFresh website** (search “CalFresh + *your county*”).
- You can also call the **county CalFresh hotline** (the number is on the website) and ask for a paper application.
3. **Submit the application**
- Upload the documents you collected, or bring them to the office if you apply in person.
4. **Interview (often by phone)**
- A county worker will call to verify information. This call usually happens **within a few days** of your submission.
5. **Decision**
- If you qualify, you’ll get an **Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card** that works like a debit card.
- First benefits can be loaded as soon as **one week after approval** in many counties.
### What If You Move Counties?
- **Tell your current county** you’re moving. They’ll close the case and send a transfer file to the new county.
- **Apply quickly** in the new county (usually the same forms).
- Bring the same documents listed above, plus a **letter from your mom** confirming you’ll live with her and the new address.

You can definitely apply for CalFresh if you just lost your job. If your income recently stopped, your county will only count any final payments you got in the last 30 days to calculate how much CalFresh you will receive in the first month. If you still have any income, your ongoing benefits will be based only on that income, not income that has stopped. You should provide proof of any money you got in the last 30 days if you can.

It isn't required, but it can be helpful to provide any proof you have that your income has stopped. This could be a letter, or a screenshot of an email or text from your employer that explains that you are no longer working. If you can’t get proof, write a letter that explains that you aren’t working. Make sure to include the last date you worked, and sign and date it.
